Title: Quantitative Equity Data Analyst
Description:
We are looking for a Data Analyst to join our Quantitative Equity Team! We are a high-performance team embedded in a top-performing quantitative equity fund that manages over $78+ billion USD in financial assets. We are dedicated to the mission-critical operation of our investment engine—a well-tuned machine responsible for generating key decisions that drive trades and investment insights. Leveraging data analytics, finance knowledge and cutting-edge technology, we aim to ensure that new and useful data products are continuously ready for research.

Do you love the idea of integrating large proprietary data sources into valuable applications? Are you a wizard at transforming ‘messy reality’ into high quality data assets? As a core member of our team, you will collaborate with investment and data experts to tackle challenging problems, and to continuously expand our capabilities in data. Based on the west coast in Vancouver, we value mentorship, collaboration, and growth in a supportive and innovative environment. Join us to make a significant impact on our investment outcomes and overall success.

What You Will Do

This is an exciting full-time role for individuals who are enthusiastic about learning the quantitative equity investment management business and excited to tackle a broad range of data, investment, and technology challenges.

You will start with a comprehensive training program, learning about various elements of quantitative equity investment management and our investment process.

You will then continue to a specialized role utilizing data analytics and data science skillsets to enable the Quantitative Equity Team’s research. Your role will involve identifying and assessing brand new data, data exploration, and proposing robust ways to integrate data products from many sources.

You will be supported with coaching and mentorship from senior members of the team, and we will create the conditions for you to grow your career steadily over time. This is an opportunity for ambitious individuals

to drive their career growth in data.

Role

While we take the approach of tailoring the career path to individual strengths, we expect successful candidates for this role to develop excellence in the following tasks:


Create processes to assess, explore, and link billions of data points.
Test structured and unstructured data sets for data quality and reliability.
Assess new data opportunities for quality and usefulness.
Evaluate your data solutions for sensibility, accuracy, and bias.
Collaborate with quantitative researchers – support alpha projects with your data expertise.
Collaborate with technology specialists – help trade off application performance and operational feasibility.
Support production deployments of your work to ensure long-term reliability.
Enable clarity of and access to your work through robust documentation and exposition.
Present findings and recommendations to key stakeholders in a clear, concise, and compelling manner.


What You Bring


Analytical Mindset – You think critically and creatively and are adept at balancing intuition with statistical validation.
Financial Knowledge – Desire to acquire the financial context needed to understand your stakeholders and make data decisions with impact.
Self-Starter – You are motivated and willing to take personal accountability for quality and timeliness of work.
Collaborative Approach – You thrive in a collaborative environment and value shared success. You proactively solicit and provide input and excel at communicating complex and technical concepts.
Time Management – You are able to manage and prioritize multiple ongoing projects.
Academic Training – At a minimum, an undergraduate degree in finance, mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, or related discipline. Completion of a relevant graduate degree is considered an asset.


We welcome applications from candidates with different levels of experience, including interns, new graduates, and experienced professionals. The base salary range for full-time roles is $125,000 – $200,000 annually plus a competitive performance bonus. Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications.

To apply for this position, please submit your resume, cover letter and academic transcripts.

Learn more by exploring our website: www.cclimq.com

We are committed to providing an inclusive, accessible recruitment and selection process. We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process. Please contact talentacquisition@cclgroup.com if you require accommodation.

AI may be used to support certain stages of our screening & recruitment process. These tools support, but do not replace, human judgment and decision-making.

Title: Operations Reporting Analyst
Description:
Branch: Gas

Affiliation: MoveUP

Employment Status: Full-Time Regular

Salary: $3,478.00 bi-weekly

Short-term Incentive Eligible: No

Workplace Flexibility: No

Posting End Date: Open until filled

As the province’s largest energy provider with more than 100 years of knowledge and experience, we proudly deliver renewable energy, natural gas, electricity and propane to 1.3 million customers.

We're actively seeking new talent to join our mission of delivering a stronger energy future in B.C. As one of BC's Top Employers with a diverse team of over 2,700 employees, we are committed to a safe and inclusive culture where each of us can connect, belong, and grow. Join us, and together, let's shape a brighter future for B.C.

Position Overview

Are you passionate about transforming complex operational data into meaningful insights? As an Operations Reporting Analyst, you'll play a key role in helping leaders make informed business decisions by analyzing operational performance, identifying trends, and developing reporting solutions that drive continuous improvement.

In this role, you'll partner with cross-functional teams to deliver impactful reporting, benchmarking, and analytical insights that support operational excellence and strategic planning.

In this role, you will


Analyze operational metrics, activities, and costs to identify trends, variances, and opportunities for improvement.
Develop, maintain, and enhance ERP-based reports and queries that support business operations and decision-making.
Conduct benchmarking, cost, and performance analyses to help establish targets and evaluate operational results.
Perform trend analysis, forecasting, and scenario modeling to assess potential business impacts and support strategic planning.
Partner with business stakeholders to understand reporting needs, investigate data gaps, and deliver actionable insights.
Present findings and recommendations that improve reporting practices, processes, and operational performance.
Support continuous improvement initiatives, system enhancements, and implementation projects.
Create training materials and procedural documentation that help users effectively understand and utilize reporting tools.


Requirements


Education: Successful completion of Diploma in Accounting, Finance, or a related field from an accredited post-secondary institution.
Experience: Minimum of six (6) years’ experience of recent and related experience, of which one year experience involves complex data analytics.
Strong analytical skills including the ability to organize, interpret and present data through reports, summaries and procedural documentation.
Excellent organizational skills, initiative and ability to balance priorities and meet deadlines.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, cost-benefit analysis and related analytical techniques.
Advanced knowledge of ERP financial systems (e.g. SAP) and reporting tools (including SAP BW) used to support cost accounting as well as other specialized software used within the department.
Ability to work with limited supervision and direction.
Strong interpersonal, presentation, verbal and written communication skills.


Our engaging workplace offers a wide range of challenging opportunities, while being safe, inclusive, and diverse. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, while supporting life-long career development. We also encourage volunteerism and nourish the need to give back to your community.

Title: Business Analyst
Description:
Company Description White Spot Limited is headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia and serves more than 15 million guests annually through its White Spot Restaurants and Triple O’s brands. White Spot operates in British Columbia; Triple O’s has operations in British Columbia, Alberta and Hong Kong. White Spot Limited is proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Best Managed Companies for the past sixteen consecutive years, achieving Platinum status.




White Spot is currently seeking a Business Analyst to strengthen our operations. The Business Analyst will be instrumental in recommending practical solutions based on their analytical findings.




Role Description As an integral member of the Business Intelligence (BI) Data Team, the Operational Business Analyst will leverage data to optimize operational performance and support strategic decision-making. Reporting to Operations, this role involves analyzing data to identify trends, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement. The analyst will build and maintain dashboards, conduct root-cause analyses, develop predictive models, and provide actionable recommendations to enhance efficiency and resource allocation. By ensuring data accuracy, aligning with governance standards, and fostering a data-driven culture, the Business Analyst will directly contribute to the success of the organization.




Salary Range

$70,000 to $80,000 annually to start, depending on experience, with potential to grow, comprehensive benefits package.




Key Responsibilities

Build and maintain dashboards and reports to track key performance indicators (KPIs)
Analyze operational data to identify trends, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement
Provide actionable recommendations to improve operational performance
Work closely with the Directors of Operations to align data insights with business priorities and operational goals
Partner with operations teams to identify data requirements, implement tracking mechanisms, and support performance improvement initiatives
Conduct root-cause analysis of operational challenges and make recommendations based on data
Develop predictive models to forecast operational performance and guide resource allocation
Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of operational programs
Collaborate with the BI Data Team to ensure that operational data is aligned with enterprise-wide data governance policies
Support the integration of operational data into organizational data warehouses and BI platforms
Maintain the accuracy and consistency of operational data
Provide regular updates and insights to leadership on operational trends, challenges, and successes
Benchmark operational metrics against industry standards to identify areas for competitive improvement
Train operations staff on data tools and dashboards to foster a data-driven culture within the department
Act as the primary point of contact for operations-related data inquiries and ad-hoc analysis requests
Support the Data Team as needed with ad hoc requests and projects




Key Attributes

Degree in business analysis, computer science, or a related field, complemented by at least 2 years of relevant professional experience 
Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools such as Excel, Tableau, or Power BI
Hands-on experience with SQL and Python for data manipulation and analysis
Hands-on experience with Snowflake an asset
Knowledge of operational KPIs and experience working with operational data systems (e.g., point-of-sale, inventory & labour management)
Strong statistical and modeling skills for forecasting and performance evaluation
Skilled at creating visual representations of data to clearly and effectively convey insights
Familiarity with data governance best practices
Robust analytical and problem-solving abilities
Excellent communication and collaboration skills
Meticulous attention to detail coupled with a dedication to data accuracy
Proven capability to work autonomously and effectively manage multiple priorities
Endless curiosity!




Preferred Qualifications

Certifications: CDMP (DAMA), CBAP, CCBA, AAC (IIBA), or equivalent are a plus.
Project Management: Experience in an Agile work environment and knowledge of change management methodologies.
Industry Knowledge: Having a solid grasp of the hospitality industry’s dynamics and the ability to connect data with business problem-solving is important. While knowledge can be gained on the job, initial familiarity is beneficial.

Description:
FNHA Overview

The First Nations Health Authority is a diverse and transformational health organization of professional, innovative, and dedicated team members and leaders.

The first of its kind in Canada, FNHA works as a health-and-wellness partner with BC First Nations to support self-determination and decision-making to improve health outcomes.

The First Nations Health Authority is committed to respecting diversity within our workforce; preference will be given to individuals who identify as First Nations, Inuit, or Métis. All interested First Nations, Inuit or Métis individuals are encouraged to apply. The First Nations Health Authority has a mandate to increase First Nations, Inuit or Métis representation in the workforce. Applicant skills, perspectives and lived experience may be matched for this role, or other opportunities within the FNHA.

FNHA is proud to have been named one of BC’s Top Employers for 2026. Learn more about why we were selected here .

Title: Senior Analyst, Primary Health Care Knowledge Development and Application

Salary: $91,172 - $ 101,898- $123,351 per year (pay range explained below)

Contract: Permanent

Hours: 8:00am-4pm Mon-Fri, flexible (core hours 9am-3pm Mon-Fri)

Location: Alberni office, Metro Vancouver located on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Coast Salish Peoples, including the territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil- Waututh Nations.

About The Role

As a Senior Analyst, Primary Health Care, your role will support FNHA in telling the story of primary health care initiatives, including the First Nations-led Primary Health Care Initiative (FNPCI). This role is responsible for developing, designing, and implementing analytical products and creating information reports for the provincial Primary Health Care team, and key reports and knowledge development products in collaboration with regional teams and other departments within FNHA.

About You

To be successful in this role you will have;

Education & Occupational Certification, Experience


An undergraduate degree from a recognized post-secondary institution is required in a related field such as health policy, public policy, health systems management, political or social science or an equivalent combination of education and experience. (Masters preferred.)
Significant, recent and relevant experience working in a primary care or primary health care setting or environment
Significant, recent and relevant experience working in or with First Nations communities and leadership
Significant, recent and relevant experience working in or with rural and remote communities


Skills/Experience


Coordinates and compiles reporting aligned with internal and external reporting requirements, and maintains and addresses issues related tracking
Extracts and presents complex datasets and analytical reports to community, management, and program experts
Presents data and findings in a variety of means, including but not limited to charts, graphs, interactive dashboards, and written reports


Please refer to Job Specification section of the Job Description for more details.

Working at FNHA

As a member of the team, you will have access to a wide range of employee benefits, including:


Municipal Pension plan with an employer contribution of 9.31%
3 weeks’ vacation, which increases with service to 4 weeks, plus 5 personal days, 1 volunteer day, and 14 public holidays including National Indigenous People’s Day, National Day of Truth and Reconciliation, Easter Monday and Boxing Day
5 cultural days per year for non-union First Nations, Inuit, or Métis employees
Access to group health benefits and a Health Care Spending Account through Canada Life on day 1 of employment
And more!


Leading with culture, all FNHA employees complete San’yas Indigenous Cultural Safety Training. We support our family to be leaders in wellness and all staff members develop a yearly wellness plan as part of their performance partnership and goal-setting.

Incumbents are typically hired, transferred or promoted between the minimum and midpoint of the range based on their knowledge, skills, abilities and experience in relation to the role requirements.

The top 10% of the pay range is for the incumbents who are industry experts in the job with the combination of exceptional experience and competencies needed to perform all duties and responsibilities at a superior capability level. Internal employee compensation will be determined as per the FNHA Employee Total Compensation Policy.

Title: Data Analyst, Investment Data Management
Description:
Interested in joining one of Canada’s top performing asset managers? We are looking for a Data Analyst for an existing vacancy on our Investment Data Management (IDM) team. The IDM Team resides within the middle office and is responsible for managing data centric processes and data quality that supports the investment management business. Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group Ltd. (CCLFG) manages a wide range of global assets and heavily relies on the output of the Data Management Team for a variety of functions from the front office to the back. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of a dynamic strategic team whose scope and importance continues to grow enterprise wide. We place a high value on maintaining an entrepreneurial spirit and creating a culture where each of us has opportunities to succeed. We are a solution orientated and collaborative team seeking like-minded individuals who thrive in a challenging and dynamic environment. Our offices currently operate on a hybrid model with a combination of in-office and remote working days throughout the week.

What You Will Do


Maintain and validate accuracy of equity/fixed income/derivative data across multiple systems/databases to enable Investment Manager modeling, trading, and risk monitoring.
Manage and enable a myriad of scheduled processes for vendor systems, internal and market data transfers, valuation, and benchmarking data inputs to the investment process.
Deliver timely data signoffs to investment teams; develop and analyze data-quality exceptions and ensure timely resolution.
Provide analysis on operational needs, ad-hoc data/data-history requests for multiple business partners to support pre- and post-trade portfolio management functions.
Identify process/workflow improvements to increase operational efficiency, mitigate risk, improve data-quality, and increase service levels provided to stakeholders.
Supporter of other operational or engineering staff, senior or managers on a variety of ad-hoc tasks and projects.


What You Bring


You have a degree in Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, Business Operations, or a related field. Relevant designation, such as the MBA, CFA, or FRM is an asset.
2-6 years of relevant experience in the investment management industry with exposure to securities data, data quality and process management. Hands-on experience working with Bloomberg, FTSE, ICE Bond Edge, Charles River and related financial tools, platforms is an asset
You possess an analytical mindset and able to break down complex processes into components to logically deduce the root cause of issues in data and technology.
You have a collaborative spirit that helps you to work well with others and you communicate effectively to team/cross-team members, and upward to key stakeholders.
You have a passion for advancing the quality, scale, and efficiency of data processes and can take ownership of multiple processes with keen attention to detail.
You constantly take a critical eye to processes with the goal of finding improvement opportunities and bring an ability to manage multiple projects.


The salary range for this position is $60,000-$90,000. The salary range provided reflects the base salary range for this position as required by legislation. In addition, there is an annual performance bonus which contributes to the total compensation for this position. Further questions may be directed to the HR team during the interview process.

Title: Business Advisor, Data and Analytics
Description:
Come work as a Business Advisor, Data & Analytics with Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH)!

Vancouver Coastal Health is looking for a Business Advisor, Data & Analytics to join the Health Analytics Team. Apply today to join our team!

As a Business Advisor, Data & Analytics with Vancouver Coastal Health you will:


Examine and interpret organizational data to unlock valuable insights to inform strategic decision-making.
Support the department’s mission to enhance data-driven decision processes, identify meaningful trends, and contribute significantly to the improvement of our business operations.
Collaborate with partners across the organization to understand and gather data requirements.
Build and applies effective data models to support business objectives.
Utilize a variety of analytical tools and techniques to generate comprehensive reports and visualizations.
Analyze complex data sets to provide useful insights into business outcomes.
Contribute to the development and execution of data-driven strategies for business optimization.
Ensure data accuracy and integrity across all analytical activities.
Keep up with industry developments and innovations in data analytics and business intelligence tools.
Carry out responsibilities in accordance with health and safety requirements.
Immediately report unsafe situations by notifying supervisor or other appropriate personnel.
Perform other related duties as assigned.


This work is framed within VCH’s commitments to our pillars of Indigenous Cultural Safety, Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, and Planetary Health.

The hours of work including days off and work area may be subject to change consistent with operational requirements and the provision of the Collective Agreement and applicable statutes. Successful applicants may be required to complete a Criminal Records Review Check.

As per Ministry of Health policy, all health care workers working in publicly-funded health care facilities are required to report their past receipt of certain vaccines or history of certain infections. Collecting these records will allow for offering of any missing vaccines, and for appropriate actions to be taken in the event of any future exposure to a communicable disease or during outbreaks. For all new hires and appointments to Vancouver Coastal Health, you will be asked to provide this information as part of the onboarding process.

Why Join Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH)

VCH is a world class innovator in medical care, research and teaching, delivering service to more than one million BC residents. At VCH, we embrace thinking boldly, taking smart risks, and 'going first' when we believe it will lead to the best possible outcomes for patients and their families. We invite you to join us in creating healthy lives in healthy communities by showcasing our passion for care, connection to the communities we serve and our culture of teamwork that makes VCH a great place to work.


Comprehensive health benefits package, including MSP, extended health and dental and municipal pension plan
Grow your career with employer-paid training and leadership development opportunities
Wellness supports, including counselling, critical incident and innovative wellness services are available to employees and their immediate families
Award-winning recognition programs to honour staff, medical staff and volunteers
Access to exclusive discount offers and deals for VCH staff


At Vancouver Coastal Health, our vision of healthy lives in healthy communities inspires us and our values and pillars guide us. We support equitable practices, diverse teams and inclusive environments, which are vital to creating welcoming spaces where everyone can bring their whole selves to work and feel supported. We encourage applications from equity-deserving communities, including Indigenous Peoples and members of racialized groups, people with disabilities and people of all gender identities and expressions and sexual orientation.

Vancouver Coastal Health is proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers, BC’s Top Employers, Canada’s Best Diversity Employers and Canada's Top Employers for Young People in 2026.

Only short-listed applicants will be contacted for this posting.

***Employees of VCH must apply online via the Internal Career Portal on CareerHub, you are currently viewing the External Career Portal. Refer to the https://my.vch.ca/working-here/job-postings site for instructions on how to view internal job postings and how to apply as an employee. Current VCH employees who apply to this posting using this external site will be considered as an external candidate. Seniority will not apply.***

Thank you for your interest in Vancouver Coastal Health.

Education & Experience


Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Business Administration, or related field, with a minimum of three (3) years’ recent, related experience in data analysis, business analytics, or a similar role, with a preference for experience in the healthcare sector or in organizations of comparable complexity. Demonstrated ability to apply data modelling, analysis, and visualization techniques in a business context.


Knowledge & Abilities


Proven experience in data analysis, business analytics, or a similar role.
Advanced proficiency in analytical tools and software (e.g., SQL, Python, R, Tableau, Power BI).
Knowledge of database systems like MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, or MS SQL
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to think analytically.
Familiarity with machine learning algorithms and predictive modeling, capable of applying these techniques to forecast trends and inform strategic decisions. Strong understanding of data privacy and security principles, especially relevant in the healthcare industry, to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of sensitive information.
Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to translate complex data into understandable insights and recommendations for non-technical stakeholders.
Experience in stakeholder management, with a demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with various departments and communicate complex data insights to non-technical audiences effectively.
A collaborative team player with a proven track record of working effectively with cross-functional teams.
Detail-oriented with a strong commitment to accuracy and quality.
Develops and maintains strong relationships with key internal and external partners to promote and enhance services provided with sensitivity to diversity and indigenous lens.
Practices the recognition, inclusion and support of all types and aspects of diversity at all stages of engagement, with an understanding of the issues faced by people from equity-deserving groups.
Physical ability to perform the duties of the position.

Title: Senior Decision Science Analyst
Description:
Come join Pattison Food Group Ltd., a Jim Pattison business, and Canada’s largest Western-based provider of food and health products.

Pattison Food Group Ltd. is a certified Great Place to Work® and consists of Save-On-Foods and other well-known grocery banners. With nearly 300 retail locations, we proudly employ nearly 30,000 team members.

We have an exciting opportunity for a full-time Senior Decision Science Analyst to join our More Rewards team in Langley, BC.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Customer Data & Analytics, you will be responsible for leveraging all aspects of data and analytics to drive large-scale projects and continuous experimentation initiatives, guiding decision-making and delivering high-quality insights. In this role, you will support the development and management of customer data and insights using a large and comprehensive dataset to support the More Rewards Loyalty Program, Retail Operations, Marketing and Merchandising.

You will be responsible for:


Collaborating with stakeholders to understand business questions, processes, and KPIs.
Formulating testable hypotheses aligned with business questions and conducting statistical experiments in a live environment.
Writing SQL scripts to automate data pipelines and workflows.
Using Python scripts in a Jupyter Notebook environment for data analysis, data wrangling, statistical testing, and predictive modeling.
Mentoring and cross-training data analysts in experimentation best practices and statistical design.
Developing dashboards and visualizations in Power BI to convey insights and report on KPIs and test results.
Working in cloud-based analytics environments and with big data tools to build analytics workflows on large datasets.
Collaborating with IT and Data Scientists to identify technical and data requirements for deploying analytic solutions tailored to business needs.
Discovering unique and creative insights to identify new opportunities for driving business value.
Becoming an expert in the relevant datasets within your analytics domain.



You have:


A degree in a STEM discipline and at least 5 years of relevant experience in data analytics or data science.
Advanced Python coding skills.
Advanced understanding of SQL.
Experience using experimental design principles, such as A/B and multivariate testing, and working with business stakeholders to formulate testable hypotheses.
Understanding of advanced analytics and data science methods such as anomaly detection, forecasting, and supervised and unsupervised learning.
Experience with visualization and reporting tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
Working knowledge of cloud environments such as Azure, GCP, or AWS.
Experience with big data tools such as Spark and Databricks and other programming languages is an asset.



You are:


A confident communicator, both verbally and in writing, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate a story with data and insights to non-technical stakeholders.
A problem-solver with strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
Effective in task management and delivering high-quality work.
Capable of multitasking and thriving in a fast-paced environment.
Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Able to mentor and guide junior team members, fostering their professional growth and enhancing team performance.



What we offer:

In addition to a highly competitive salary, we offer a great range of benefits, a company pension plan, free parking, on-site gym, exclusive team member offers, and opportunities for development and career progression.

If you’re looking to join a team that puts people first, you’re in the right place. Apply online today!

Compensation Details:

$96,443.00 - $120,554.00

The compensation offered for this position will take into consideration location, education, skills, experience and other factors.

Title: Data Analyst, BC Children's Hospital Research
Description:
Data Analyst

BC Children's Hospital Research

Vancouver, BC

In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of Provincial Health Services Authority patient safety is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA, and as such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.

Reporting to Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation, the Data Analyst is responsible for coordinating CHBC data requests, performing data extraction and complex data transformations, preparing information reports and collaborative analyses, performing data quality checking and documentation from various provincial datasets. This includes regular data quality monitoring, preparing data for analysis, and generating reports for the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA), the Ministry of Health (MoH), and care providers in the Health Authorities within British Columbia. This position supports monitoring of CHBC initiatives and provincial child health service performance indicators for use in the planning, implementation and evaluation of child and youth health care in the province. This position provides support to the CHBC Executive Director, and CHBC Leads and team members in performing management of data, analysis and reports. The Data Analyst advises others within the organization of the potential impacts of the specific data requirements of Data Sharing Agreements (DSA) and Information Sharing Plans (ISP) being executed and anticipates questions in order to problem solve in the process of due diligence.

What You’ll Do


Support for internal and external child and youth data needs to support evidence-based decision making, systems planning and policy-making as well as evaluation and research purposes by performing duties including: review of data availability, data extraction, data quality checking and cleaning, data manipulation and merging, and information summaries.
Develop complex data extraction and transformation scripts, including data linkages, to prepare data for analysis. Perform analysis and prepare reports and other analytical products (e.g. dashboards, scorecards). Implement indicators for monitoring and regular reporting.
Assist CHBC leadership team in the development of DSAs and ISPs to ensure the security of shared records and patient privacy.
Prepare a variety of materials including: confidential reports and correspondence, agreements, project outlines, meeting minutes and agendas with guidance Director of Quality Improvement, Evaluation and Projects to develop the Information Sharing Plan (ISP) and communicates with MoH or other data sources for data linkage. Link data sources from PHSA databases with other major health information systems such as the MoH hospital discharge database, Pharmanet, Medical Services Plan, and Vital Statistics. Take measures to protect all data and information sources to comply with protection of confidentiality and privacy policies.
Produce regular and ad hoc reports that monitor and benchmark cost, utilization and other quality and performance indicators for selected child services in BC and communicate findings to PHSA staff and external stakeholders at the local, regional, provincial and national levels.
Assist the development of a data quality and change management plan and related strategies to identify and implement prospective and concurrent methods to avoid, reduce and rectify data quality issues.
Provide support for the development and maintenance of data collection and recording systems such as databases, spreadsheets and web sites, including the design of standard and ad hoc reports. Write computer code and data queries to extract, capture and edit data.
Identify learning needs that contribute to skill enhancement and career progression for self and foster a working environment that stimulate learning and inquiry for the team. Take responsibility for keeping up-to-date on new initiatives, developments and trends in child health information sciences. Communicate information and make recommendations to the Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation for evaluation and approval.


Qualifications

What you bring


A level of education, training, and experience equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Biostatistics or Health Informatics and one to three years of experience in health care organizations.
Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within BC Children's Hospital Research contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.


Core Competencies


Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).


Skills & Knowledge


Demonstrated ability to perform database querying, advanced data manipulation, analysis and information presentation through using relational database and statistical software. Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing. Demonstrated ability to use Microsoft operating systems, Excel, Access, Word. Demonstrated ability to use statistical software, such as SAS or R. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills including the ability to comprehend complex issues, related data/information, and present information in concise meaningful ways. Demonstrated organization skills to generate work plans to handle multiple concurrent tasks, meet project deadlines within timeline, scope and budget. Physical ability to perform the duties of the job. Ability to understand and interpret data management concepts and processes and communicate complex ideas in simple terminology. Ability to develop complex and customized queries and reports. Ability to collaborate and work within a team while working independently.
Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.


What We Bring

Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. Whether you are providing direct care, conducting research, or making it possible for others to do their work, you impact the lives of British Columbians today and in the future. BC Children's Hospital Research

Vancouver, BC

In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of Provincial Health Services Authority patient safety is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA, and as such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.

Reporting to Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation, the Data Analyst is responsible for coordinating CHBC data requests, performing data extraction and complex data transformations, preparing information reports and collaborative analyses, performing data quality checking and documentation from various provincial datasets. This includes regular data quality monitoring, preparing data for analysis, and generating reports for the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA), the Ministry of Health (MoH), and care providers in the Health Authorities within British Columbia. This position supports monitoring of CHBC initiatives and provincial child health service performance indicators for use in the planning, implementation and evaluation of child and youth health care in the province. This position provides support to the CHBC Executive Director, and CHBC Leads and team members in performing management of data, analysis and reports. The Data Analyst advises others within the organization of the potential impacts of the specific data requirements of Data Sharing Agreements (DSA) and Information Sharing Plans (ISP) being executed and anticipates questions in order to problem solve in the process of due diligence.

What You’ll Do

  • Support for internal and external child and youth data needs to support evidence-based decision making, systems planning and policy-making as well as evaluation and research purposes by performing duties including: review of data availability, data extraction, data quality checking and cleaning, data manipulation and merging, and information summaries.
  • Develop complex data extraction and transformation scripts, including data linkages, to prepare data for analysis. Perform analysis and prepare reports and other analytical products (e.g. dashboards, scorecards). Implement indicators for monitoring and regular reporting.
  • Assist CHBC leadership team in the development of DSAs and ISPs to ensure the security of shared records and patient privacy.
  • Prepare a variety of materials including: confidential reports and correspondence, agreements, project outlines, meeting minutes and agendas with guidance Director of Quality Improvement, Evaluation and Projects to develop the Information Sharing Plan (ISP) and communicates with MoH or other data sources for data linkage. Link data sources from PHSA databases with other major health information systems such as the MoH hospital discharge database, Pharmanet, Medical Services Plan, and Vital Statistics. Take measures to protect all data and information sources to comply with protection of confidentiality and privacy policies.
  • Produce regular and ad hoc reports that monitor and benchmark cost, utilization and other quality and performance indicators for selected child services in BC and communicate findings to PHSA staff and external stakeholders at the local, regional, provincial and national levels.
  • Assist the development of a data quality and change management plan and related strategies to identify and implement prospective and concurrent methods to avoid, reduce and rectify data quality issues.
  • Provide support for the development and maintenance of data collection and recording systems such as databases, spreadsheets and web sites, including the design of standard and ad hoc reports. Write computer code and data queries to extract, capture and edit data.
  • Identify learning needs that contribute to skill enhancement and career progression for self and foster a working environment that stimulate learning and inquiry for the team. Take responsibility for keeping up-to-date on new initiatives, developments and trends in child health information sciences. Communicate information and make recommendations to the Director, Quality Improvement and Evaluation for evaluation and approval.

Title: Data Analyst - Portfolio Reporting, Real Estate Debt
Description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description:

The Data Analyst - Portfolio Reporting, Real Estate Debt (12 month Contract) will report directly to the Director, Portfolio Reporting, Real Estate Debt. We are seeking a highly motivated individual with a background in Data Science or Data Analytics who is looking to develop their career in an entrepreneurial and high-energy environment. Embedded within the business, this role supports management reporting, forecasting, and portfolio analysis across the RE Debt portfolio, in addition to being the primary liaison to ED&A and IT — translating reporting requirements into data specifications and building data flows from the Enterprise Data Platform through to the reporting layer. This position also works closely with the Real Estate Debt Investment, Accounting, and Operations teams, FP&A, and Portfolio Management teams across QuadReal.

Role Description:


Support scenario modelling, cash flow forecasting, leverage and liquidity analysis through Anaplan, supplemented by ad-hoc financial models as needed, using AI-assisted development for efficiency and quality control
Analyze portfolio exposures, return attribution, and market trends, and support the development of presentation materials with AIenhanced insights and visualization
Assist in the preparation of monthly, quarterly and ad hoc management reports for senior management, Board of Directors and BCI
Support real estate debt investment underwriting by providing portfolio impact analysis
Assist with ad hoc research projects for benchmarking, peer analysis, risk analysis, and other relevant topics
Query and extract data from enterprise data platforms to support portfolio reporting and analytics needs
Develop and maintain business logic, portfolio calculations, and data transformation rules that underpin reporting outputs
Serve as the primary business-side liaison to IT and ED&A, translating reporting requirements into data specifications and validating platform outputs
Support data enablement initiatives and ongoing data management and governance priorities across the RE Debt portfolio
Validate and reconcile data collected from different systems using AI-powered anomaly detection to improve data quality and identify process improvement opportunities


Experience And Qualifications:


University degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. Statistics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field) OR a background in Economics, Finance or a related business field. CFA or similar designation is a plus
2–3 years of experience working in a data analyst role, ideally in investment management or real estate.
Analytical – Strong quantitative and analytical skills; detail-oriented and proficient in building and handling complicated data sets.
Excellent communication and presentation skills; demonstrates an ability to effectively communicate and present results that articulate key themes and messages.
Must be able to allocate time effectively and work under pressure to meet tight deadlines, handle multiple demands and competing priorities, and adapt to new ideas and change. Comfortable following direction but also contributing to the direction.
Advanced knowledge of SQL, Power Query, Excel, and Power BI is required. Familiarity with Anaplan or a similar planning tool is an asset. Experience with Tableau or Python is considered a plus.
Proactive approach to leveraging technology for process improvement and analytical enhancement. Comfortable learning and applying new tools, automation techniques, GenAI applications (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot), and advanced analytics platforms to solve complex problems, automate data analysis, rapidly prototype financial models, and deliver higher-quality insights.
Has a questioning frame of mind, asks “why” and challenges the status quo with improvements to drive change when needed.


The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $74,000-$84,000.

The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity.

We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) technology — alongside human review — to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. Our recruitment team remains involved in all decisions.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada as the company does not provide work permit sponsorship for this role.

Note to Recruiters: QuadReal does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to QuadReal, directly or indirectly, will be considered QuadReal property. QuadReal will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. A recruiting agency must first have a valid, written and fully executed agency agreement contract for engaged services to submit resumes.

QuadReal Property Group will provide reasonable accommodation at any time throughout the hiring process for applicants with disabilities or for those needing job postings in an alternate format. If you require accommodation, please advise the Talent Acquisition team member you are working with and include the following: Job posting #, your name and your preferred method of contact.

Title: Portfolio Intelligence Analyst
Description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON / Vancouver, BC; Hybrid

About The Role

The Portfolio Intelligence Analyst is responsible for producing trusted portfolio intelligence that enables effective enterprise portfolio management and informed executive decision-making. Reporting to the Enterprise Portfolio Manager, the role gathers, validates, analyses and maintains portfolio information across the enterprise technology portfolio. The Portfolio Intelligence Analyst develops executive dashboards, portfolio analytics, governance information and performance reporting while supporting portfolio planning, investment prioritization, and ongoing portfolio monitoring.

The role ensures portfolio information is complete, accurate, timely, and decision-ready, providing the analytical foundation upon which portfolio governance, investment decisions and executive reporting are based.

In this role, you will…

Portfolio Analysis and Intelligence


Analyze portfolio data to support prioritization, investment planning, capacity management, financial oversight, dependency management, and portfolio health assessments.
Develop actionable insights, identify trends, risks, and data anomalies, and provide recommendations to support strategic decision-making.


Executive Reporting and Governance Support


Develop and maintain executive dashboards, scorecards, portfolio reports, governance packs, and performance metrics.
Support governance forums by preparing briefing materials, decision-support information, meeting documentation, and tracking governance actions and outcomes.
Ensure reporting is timely, accurate, consistent, and tailored for executive audiences.


Business Case and Investment Support


Support business case intake, validation, investment appraisal, and enterprise portfolio prioritization activities.
Maintain business case repositories and associated supporting documentation.


Portfolio Health Monitoring & Continuous Improvement


Monitor portfolio financial performance, resource utilization, delivery health, risks, dependencies, benefits realization, and key portfolio metrics.
Maintain high standards of data quality and information integrity across the portfolio.
Identify and implement improvements to portfolio analytics, reporting, processes, automation, and AI-enabled portfolio intelligence capabilities.


What You Bring


Basic / Minimum Education requirement to perform the job: Bachelor's degree
Preferred educational requirements to perform the job:
Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP)
SAFe® Lean Portfolio Management (LPM)
SAFe® Product Owner/Product Manager (POPM)
Kanban Management Professional (KMP)
Management of Portfolios (MoP®)
PRINCE2® Foundation
Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300)
Relevant Years of experience required to perform the role: 3 to 5 yrs of experience
Experience working within project, program, or Agile frameworks is an asset and preferred
Commercial Real Estate experience / background to perform the role is preferred

Pursuant to local law, Colliers is disclosing the following information:

Area/Location Specific: Toronto, ON & Vancouver, BC

Description:
Job Description

As an Associate Analyst - Inventory you will be focused on inventory analysis and/or execution of strategies and processes to ensure that inventory and service levels are optimized.

Responsibilities


Executes accurate, scheduled daily, weekly, and monthly reports.
Reconciles report data to ensure data integrity.
Audits processing errors or bad data points before releasing reports.
Maintains report contact database, controls user access to shared network drives and other common resources, and executes regular backups.
Maintains production reports, makes approved changes to report data by modifying Teradata SQL, formatting Excel macros, and Access databases.
Executes on demand processes and reports, adjusts input parameters, data, and formatting prior to execution, and validates report data prior to publishing results.
Assists in ad-hoc report development and execution, including modifying existing or developing new SQL, running reports, and formatting data using advanced Excel capabilities.
Prepares and analyzes data for various projects and initiatives, including interpreting and summarizing findings in PowerPoint or Microsoft Word format.


Qualifications


High School Degree or equivalent experience required. Bachelor’s degree in business related field preferred.
4-year degree or equivalent combination of education and work experience
Ability to follow established processes and schedule to deliver timely and consistent report execution.
Ability to work independently, check your results, troubleshoot problems and exercise judgment.
Expert knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including creating and editing macros and utilizing other advanced functionality.
Knowledge of Microsoft Access, including creating basic queries, code and reports.
Understanding of relational databases, including creating SQL statements.
Knowledge of other applications, including Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Outlook.
Excellent analytical and problem solving skills, proven ability to apply these in business environment.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to lift up to 50lbs.
Ability and willingness to work in the warehouse/yard.
1 year forklift experience preferred.
Knowledge of distribution industry, supply chain, purchasing, and inventory concepts, practices, and procedures.

Title: Pricing Analyst
Description:
About Us:

With over 60 years of industry experience, Gescan has 29 branches located across Western Canada. At Gescan, we leverage our strong global resource base, our local expertise, and our family-oriented values to deliver the best service to our customers and suppliers.

We are a proud member of the Sonepar Group, the world's largest privately-held electrical distributor. The Sonepar Group is present in more than 40 countries with over 45,000 employees. In Canada, we are represented by 6 locally managed electrical and industrial distributors and have over 110 locations with coverage in 9 provinces.

To explore and learn more about Sonepar opportunities, please visit www.career.sonepar.com




What’s In It For You?

You will be joining a market leader with over 40 years of experience to help you elevate your potential.
You will be working for the world's #1 privately held business to business distributor of electrical products and related solutions.
A chance to get involved in the forever growing electrical industry.
We house the largest inventory to better service our customers and deliver on sales commitments.
An opportunity for career development across many business departments within our organization.




Scope

Under the supervision of the Pricing Manager, the primary mandate of the Pricing Analyst is to analyze any trend, from products, categories, customers and suppliers. The analyst will be responsible for the creation, structure and management of the product database.




Responsibilities

Tool development
Develop dynamic pricing tools and models to effectively meet business needs.
Extract, process, and edit reports from Cognos and Power BI (Excel file, Access, pivot tables).
Perform complex analyses of our current pricing, product, vendor customer data using Excel, Power BI, Cognos, and our internal and external databases.
Analyze and interpret market trends in collaboration with internal teams for the purpose of developing competitive pricing strategies;
Analyze data from a variety of sources to better understand pricing strategies, better structure our customer types, and better aggregate our products and suppliers.
Prepare and present the results of the pricing and profitability analysis to management.
Keep abreast of different methods of price analysis, industry trends, and database management
Develop dynamic tools to improve database management.
Participate in the management of the information of the database and ensure the compliance of the information found therein and propose solutions.Team Support
Validate and approve pricing agreements on a daily basis to understand the pricing cycle and support the team as needed.
Assist the team in preparing for IT changes on products, categories, customers and suppliers.
All other related tasks.




Required

Bachelor's degree in administration or related field.
Excellent command of Microsoft Office suite tools (Excel, Access, Outlook, Teams).
Good knowledge of technological tools such as MS VBA/SQL, Python, Power BI, Power Apps.
Knowledge of Cognos (an asset). • A minimum of 1-3 years of experience in the field and/or related field.
Experience in interpretation, data analysis, database management, and dashboard creation.
Programming experience (basic).




Benefits & Perks

We offer a competitive salary, plus a full set of benefits.

Benefits program allowing you to choose from options that best fit you and your dependents’ needs. Benefit options include: Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Spending Account & RRSP matching.
Employee Assistance Program, Tuition Reimbursement, Employee Discounts and a career path.
Regardless of your benefits program, you will receive company paid Life Insurance, and employee paid disability.

Title: Business Analytics Specialist
Description:
Aviso:

At Aviso, we are dedicated to improving the financial well-being of Canadians. As a leading wealth management organization, we are committed to leadership, innovation, partnership, responsibility, and community. Working with talented and energetic professionals who exemplify our values every day, you will quickly notice that our people and dynamic ‘oneaviso' culture sets us apart. If you are looking for interesting and challenging work, at a company committed to its people, find out more about what Aviso has to offer at www.aviso.ca.

The Opportunity:

We're looking to fill an opening for a Business Analytics Specialist to join our Data Science and AI Enablement team.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Data Science and AI Enablement, you will be instrumental in supporting the business analytics functions at Aviso Wealth. Principle responsibilities include updating and distributing Business Analytics reporting and ad-hoc data mining for analysis.

As oneaviso:


We Care - You do the right thing for clients, partners and colleagues. You build trusted relationships, champion service excellence, and contribute to a culture where people feel valued and supported
We Dare -You challenge the status quo with bold ideas and fresh perspectives. You embrace change, seek opportunities to innovate and are comfortable exploring new ways of working
We Share - You collaborate openly and build meaningful relationships. You seek out diverse perspectives, share your knowledge and work together to help colleagues, clients and partners succeed
We Deliver - You take ownership of your work, honour your commitments and focus on delivering meaningful results. You hold yourself accountable and continuously look for ways to improve


What your day looks like:


Produce and distribute business reports for internal and external stakeholders, including ad‑hoc data mining across unstructured and disparate data sources.
Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and documentation of all data, reports, assumptions, and methodologies.
Serve as the Asset Management data steward, working with NEI and other providers to validate and maintain high‑quality source data for the data warehouse.
Partner with third‑party data management teams on schema changes and new solutions, including reviewing business requirements, writing technical specifications, and completing system testing.
Influence cross‑functional teams to prioritize Asset Management needs on the data services roadmap, including enhancements to legacy tools.
Apply prescriptive and predictive analytics to strengthen reporting, surface insights to senior leaders, and translate recommendations into action.
Lead research and experimentation as a squad leader to advance DNA strategy within the AI product roadmap


Requirements

Your experience and skills:


Bachelor's degree in a relevant STEM or business field; 5+ years analytics experience in Business Analytics
Certifications in AI/ML or Data Engineering
Experience utilizing Databricks to enable scalable data solutions that support analytics, reporting, and business insights
Experience in federated analytics environments (preferred)
Skilled with SQL, modern BI tools and large, diverse datasets
Working knowledge of Confluence, Jira, and DevOps practices for tracking and documentation

Si vous recherchez un poste stimulant, mais aussi très gratifiant et à fort impact, alors poursuivez votre lecture !

Responsabilités


Prendre en charge divers projets d’analyse liés au numérique, au marketing et au commerce électronique afin d’accompagner les équipes internationales à l’aide de données, de tableaux de bord et d’informations sur les éléments standards du cycle de vie des clients par abonnement, notamment l’acquisition, la fidélisation et l’expansion
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires commerciaux et les membres de l’équipe pour explorer divers sujets, tels que les opportunités de marché, les parcours sectoriels/produits, la contribution du numérique, l’entonnoir d’achat et les analyses du comportement client, afin d’en extraire des informations précieuses
Collecter, analyser et visualiser les données à l’aide d’outils permettant d’exploiter et de synthétiser efficacement les informations pour présenter un récit concis et exploitable, et communiquer des conclusions qui éclairent les décisions commerciales

3 ans ou plus d’expérience pertinente.
Solides aptitudes logiques, avec la capacité de présenter des données complexes sous forme de récits et de visualisations simples, concis et captivants qui mettent les informations clés en avant.

Qualifications Souhaitées


Solides connaissances de l’environnement numérique et marketing (e-commerce), avec une expérience des indicateurs et analyses liés au marketing, au e-commerce ou aux modèles d’abonnement
Capacité à réfléchir de manière stratégique aux problèmes commerciaux concrets dans le domaine du marketing et à les mettre en corrélation avec les données sous-jacentes afin de mener des analyses approfondies et d’identifier des solutions innovantes
Solides compétences en matière de présentation et d’expression orale, avec une expérience des présentations devant la direction
Solide expérience des outils de visualisation tels que Power BI (y compris DAX), Tableau, etc.
Solides bases en manipulation de données à l’aide de SQL ainsi que d’Excel avancé (visualisation, tableaux croisés dynamiques, etc.) ; une expérience des macros et/ou de VBA constitue un atout certain

Une expérience en modélisation analytique et dans les langages de programmation associés (R, Python) est un atout

Self-starter, who takes initiative and demonstrated success in working with and influencing stakeholders, business partners cross-functionally.

Strong experience in visualization tools such as Power BI (including DAX), Tableau etc.
Solid foundation in manipulating data using SQL as well as advanced Excel (visualization, pivot tables etc.), experience with macros and/or VBA is a definite plus

Position Highlights

ICBC’s Strategic Supply Management team is seeking a Business Analytics Consultant to provide analytical, consultative, and advisory services on corporate and divisional initiatives requiring supplier-related insights.

Key Responsibilities


Lead analyses of complex or sensitive supplier information by identifying business and supplier opportunities, evaluating data, and presenting clear recommendations to key internal stakeholders.

Design, develop, and maintain analytical models that support supplier management.
Build and maintain strong relationships with executive leaders and senior management to understand business priorities and operations and identify opportunities to improve supplier management practices.

Support strategic sourcing, category planning and management, and process-improvement activities that enhance efficiency and sustainability.


 

Position Requirements


Strong business acumen, demonstrated through advanced financial analysis and modelling, leadership of complex analytical projects, and contributions to strategic decision-making.
Proficiency in data analysis, quantitative research, and predictive modelling, with the ability to translate large, complex, and diverse datasets into actionable business insights and recommendations.
Advanced proficiency in Excel, Tableau, SQL, and either Python or R for data extraction, analysis, modelling, automation, and visualization.
Experience with AWS analytics platforms and QuickSight is an asset.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to collaborate across ICBC, frame complex problems, and influence strategic and operational decisions.
Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deliverables and adapt to changing business priorities.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
Knowledge of business performance and process-improvement principles, concepts, and techniques.
Relevant experience supported by a professional designation aligned with the role, such as an MBA, CFA, or CPA.

Description:
Location: Vancouver, BC

Duration: 12-Month Contract

Work Arrangement: Hybrid – 2–3 days per week in office

MatchBox Consulting Group is seeking a Project Performance Analyst to support one of British Columbia’s largest utility providers. This role is focused on transforming project and portfolio data into actionable insights, maintaining reliable performance reporting, improving business processes, and communicating findings to project teams and senior leadership.

The successful candidate will bring strong experience with Power BI, Excel, Power Query, data analysis, portfolio reporting, and data visualization, along with the ability to work independently with complex project performance data.

Key Responsibilities


Extract, clean, transform, and analyze project performance data from SAP-BW and other enterprise systems.
Develop and maintain reliable portfolio and project performance reporting.
Produce standardized monthly and quarterly reports as well as timely ad hoc analysis.
Build and maintain Power BI dashboards, reports, and data visualizations.
Transform complex project data into meaningful insights that support business and portfolio decision-making.
Present analytical findings and reporting results clearly to project teams, senior leaders, and other stakeholders.
Support portfolio management activities including forecast deep-dive reviews and project releases.
Identify reporting gaps and recommend improvements based on analytical findings and business requirements.
Develop repeatable and standardized reporting processes to improve efficiency and consistency.
Document operational processes, reporting procedures, and analytical activities.
Partner with technology teams to ensure systems supporting portfolio management reporting provide reliable, on-demand access to required data.
Independently investigate and resolve moderately complex reporting, data, and business process issues.
Support senior team members and Team Leads with portfolio reporting and analysis as required.


Required Qualifications


Minimum 8 years of strategic business analysis experience or equivalent.
Strong hands-on Power BI experience – this is a mandatory requirement.
Strong proficiency with Excel and Power Query.
Demonstrated experience with data analysis and data visualization.
Experience with portfolio and project reporting.
Ability to extract, organize, analyze, and communicate complex business and project information.
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving capabilities.
Experience presenting analytical findings to both project teams and senior leadership.
Strong stakeholder management, communication, and collaboration skills.
Ability to independently identify reporting gaps and develop practical solutions.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Law, Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a related discipline.
Advanced written and spoken English skills for a professional environment.


Nice to Have


Experience with SAP-BW or similar enterprise reporting/data systems.
Experience with Microsoft Dynamics.
Experience developing automated or standardized reporting processes.
Exposure to portfolio management, project performance, forecasting, or project controls environments.
Experience supporting process improvement initiatives.

Title: Managed Services Enablement and Reporting Analyst
Description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

Role Overview

The analyst develops reports, dashboards, and data-driven insights using tools such as SQL, Excel, and Power BI to monitor service delivery effectiveness, resource utilization, financial performance, and client engagement health. The role also supports business requirements gathering, testing, and validation activities related to ServiceNow enhancements and process improvements. This position is primarily execution-focused and works under the guidance of management to deliver actionable analysis and platform improvements.

Key Responsibilities

Managed Services Engagement Analytics


Collect financial and utilization data across various business platforms to aid in evaluation and optimization of managed services engagements.
Help identify trends, anomalies, and performance gaps impacting service delivery, profitability, and resource allocation.
Prepare recurring operational and financial performance reports for review by leadership.


Reporting Outputs


Create and maintain reports, dashboards, and visualizations using Power BI, Excel, SQL, and ServiceNow reporting tools.
Develop SQL queries and data extracts to support operational analysis and decision-making.
Validate data accuracy and investigate reporting discrepancies.
Assist in developing standardized reporting and KPI measurement frameworks.
Translate business questions into meaningful data analysis and reporting solutions.


ServiceNow Platform Support


Support administration and enhancement efforts within the ServiceNow platform.
Gather and document business requirements, user stories, process flows, and acceptance criteria.
Collaborate with developers and administrators to clarify requirements and validate proposed solutions.
Assist in identifying opportunities for workflow optimization and process automation.
Maintain documentation related to system functionality, business processes, and enhancement requests.


ServiceNow Testing & Validation


Develop and execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) plans and test scripts.
Validate enhancements and defect resolutions against approved requirements.
Document and track testing results, issues, and defects.
Coordinate testing activities with stakeholders and development resources.
Support release validation and post-implementation reviews.


Required Qualifications


Experience supporting, administering, or working within ServiceNow or a similar enterprise workflow platform.
Working knowledge of ServiceNow processes, data structures, reporting capabilities, and platform configuration concepts.
Ability to gather requirements, document business needs, and communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Experience conducting User Acceptance Testing (UAT), defect management, and solution validation.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and translate information into meaningful reporting or operational insights.
Basic understanding of financial metrics including revenue, cost management, profitability, and resource planning.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience working with reporting or business intelligence tools such as SQL reports and PowerBi.
Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment when working with sensitive business, operational, or employee-related data.


Working Style and Success Factors


Collaborative and service-oriented, with the ability to build effective working relationships across business, technical, and leadership audiences.
Detail-oriented and quality-focused, with a strong commitment to accurate documentation, thorough testing, and reliable reporting.
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities, timelines, and deliverables may shift based on business needs.
Curious and improvement-minded, with an interest in identifying opportunities to streamline processes, improve reporting, and enhance platform usability.
Accountable and proactive, with the ability to follow through on open items, communicate blockers, and support continuous improvement across platform operations.
Handle sensitive operational data with discretion, including charge hour tracking, service line metrics, employee platform usage, and information that may be associated with performance-related reporting.
Partner effectively with global team members, including offshore resources, to coordinate work, share knowledge, and support timely delivery across time zones.
Previous experience working in or with a professional services firm preferred.
